question.text: An institutional LP proposes an Investor Side Letter granting lower management fee and a seat on the Investment Committee. Ch 12 warns the Manager that granting side-letter rights is subject to which fundamental constraint?

answer.text: The Manager has a fiduciary duty towards OTHER investors and must ensure differential rights do not breach that fiduciary duty; preferential terms are typically effected by issuing a separate Class of Units.
Side Letters are prohibited outright by SEBI for any Category of AIF.
Side letter rights can only include lower management fee — no other preferences are permissible.
Side letters are valid only if approved by SEBI in writing before execution.

explanation.text: The Logic: Ch 12 Investor Side Letters section: 'the investment manager of an AIF has a fiduciary duty towards other investors' and should not breach it; preferential terms are delivered via separate Class of Units. The Trap: B, C, D all over-restrict or fabricate a SEBI pre-approval requirement. Cross-Exam Context: The SEBI 'equal treatment' principle echoes XXI-B (PM) and MF regulations. AIF nuance: differential treatment is allowed via Class of Units, not by secret carve-outs. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a 'Side Letter Matrix' — all concessions, triggered by commitment size thresholds. Include a 'Most Favoured Nation' clause that auto-extends LP-A's benefits to LP-B if LP-B meets the same threshold. Protects against future disputes.
